title: Diagnose and Recover Until the End of an Operation

blocks.text: Preserve Results from Complete Operations

The interpreter now accepts several operations, each terminated by ;. A valid operation produces Result: N. An invalid one produces Error: followed by its diagnostic and is discarded through its boundary; the next operation is then attempted. A result is displayed only after both the expression and its semicolon have been validated. A computed prefix of an incomplete operation is not reported as a result.

End of input between operations is normal and produces no extra line. A ; without an expression is an invalid empty operation. Newlines remain separators; they do not replace the semicolon. Each test has at most 120 ASCII characters, literals in 0..99, intermediate results in -100..100, and a maximum nesting depth of 8.

The grammar preserves unexpected tokens. If 4+; is missing its right-hand unit, the ; is held in the buffer when the diagnostic is thrown. Recovery must recognize that reserved token as the already encountered boundary; searching for another ; among the characters would lose the following operation.
Recovery Must Consume Its Own Pending State

Add the declaration bool descartar_operacion(); to the reader's public interface. The following definition belongs to Lector_tokens, as indicated by ::, so it can access the class's private members. Place it after the class definition in the file; it is not a free function that accesses those members.

If the buffer holds ;, the function empties the buffer and returns true without touching the characters of the following operation. If it holds the end marker, it consumes that marker logically and returns false. Another reserved token belongs to the rejected operation and is abandoned before searching for its terminator in the remaining characters.

The method checks bad() before changing even the buffer: a reservation must not conceal a serious failure. Clearing flags does not repair the underlying source. With prepared text, clear permits continuation after end-of-input or failure flags, and get advances one character at a time. Recovery does not call leer_token here: a character rejected by the language must be discardable without triggering the same lexical error again.
Decide What the Recovery Result Means

true means the rejected operation's ending delimiter was consumed and another operation may be attempted. false means the end of input was reached without another boundary to recover. It does not prove that another operation exists: if the semicolon was the last character, the next read simply returns end of input.

blocks.question: The buffer holds ; after a missing operand, and the remaining text begins with "9;". What must descartar_operacion do?
options: Search for the ; in 9; and discard that operation too.
Return false because a reservation prevents continuation.
Consume the reserved token, return true, and leave 9; available.
blocks.explanation: The reserve is already the terminator of the invalid operation. Consuming characters through another semicolon would lose the following operation.

blocks.text: If neither a reserved token nor a remaining semicolon exists, every successful get consumes a character, and the final attempt reaches end of input. Recovery terminates even if it encounters letters, incomplete parentheses, or numbers outside the domain. Its goal is to find a boundary, not to revalidate the discarded text.
The Outer Loop Catches One Operation per Attempt

The loop must check whether an initial unit exists. If it is the end marker, it stops. Otherwise, it returns that token for the grammar to consume. The try block covers the initial read and the operation, so errors recognizing the first character are also caught. After a diagnostic, recovery is called; a recovery failure ends the loop instead of retrying a severely damaged source.

This fragment replaces the one-operation main from the earlier file and requires the extended reader and previous grammar. The later reference integrates it into a complete program. A valid operation no longer requires an immediate end of all text: the loop allows another operation after ;. The internal rules for precedence, units, and domain remain unchanged.

blocks.question: Why is the initial token returned before leer_operacion is called?
options: To preserve it as the first unit that the grammar still needs to consume.
To erase all characters of the previous operation.
To increase the nesting limit automatically.
blocks.explanation: The loop only looked ahead to distinguish end of input from an available operation. It returns that unit because it belongs to the rule that will interpret the expression.

blocks.text: Guided Integration of Recovery

This guided integration connects the recovery method and outer loop already explained to your previous program. Trace the reader's state and verify the boundaries; building an interpreter independently from a minimal structure will be practiced later. The editor contains the previous one-operation interpreter. Extend the reader with recovery through ; and change the outer loop to process several operations. The initial text is "4+;7*2;". A diagnostic for a missing unit must appear, followed by Result: 14. Do not display the partial value 4 or discard the operation 7*2;.

Test "8/0;2+3;": reject the divisor, then display Result: 5. "100;6;": reject the numeric literal, then display 6. "(2+3;4;": reject the missing closing delimiter, then display 4. ";5;": reject an empty operation, then display 5. "2+3" should produce one diagnostic for the missing terminator and no result. "2+3;?;4;" must preserve results 5 and 4 around the lexical diagnostic.

Also test empty text or separators only: neither should create fictitious operations. A newline between a calculation and ; is allowed as a separator; a newline without ; does not terminate an operation. Preserve the previous interpreter's value range and nesting depth. Each output line must correspond to a complete result or a diagnostic; the editor does not automatically check these criteria.

Choose where to catch errors and where to recover. Trace at least one case with a reserved ;, another with a consumed invalid character, and a third that reaches the end without ;. Explain what is consumed in each case before returning to the loop. If you continually preserve the same token without stopping or advancing, recovery fails the progress requirement.
Compare After Building the Loop

The reference uses "6+;8/2;". The first diagnostic preserves its terminator and recovery consumes it from the buffer; the second operation remains available and produces 4. Character-by-character recovery permits discarding other malformed inputs without requiring the grammar to accept them again.

Compare your implementation against the criteria: the first operation produces no result, each ; is consumed exactly as the boundary of its own operation, and the following operation is interpreted from its beginning. Your exact diagnostic wording may differ if it identifies the same requirement. A serious stream failure must stop recovery; these reproducible texts do not attempt to simulate device failure.
Recover Precedence and Errors Across Other Operations

blocks.question: Predict the interpreter's complete output with an error and two subsequent calculations.
answers:
Error: Expected a unit
Result: 4
Result: 12
blocks.explanation: The semicolon in 3+; is preserved and consumed during recovery. 9/2 yields 4 by integer division; the final grouping produces 3 and is multiplied by 4.

blocks.question: Predict the diagnostic and result after an unsupported character.
blocks.explanation: The reader consumes ? and throws. Recovery discards +9; as the rest of the malformed operation; the next operation produces 4.

blocks.text: A Local Policy Preserves Other Responsibilities

blocks.question: descartar_operacion checks bad() before reading characters. Which behavior fulfills its contract?
options: Clear the flag and promise that the failure has disappeared.
Throw a recovery diagnostic and end this traversal.
Create a numeric token 0 so that a result always exists.
blocks.explanation: The method cannot repair a seriously damaged input source. It reports that condition and stops the loop rather than pretending recovery succeeded or fabricating a value.

blocks.text: Recovery does not guarantee that later input is valid: it only preserves the possibility of analyzing it from the boundary. Every new operation must again pass the unit, term, expression, domain, and terminator rules. The next construction will remove part of the provided module so that you can integrate your own decisions and test the interpreter as a program. Recovery that first examines the reserved token and then discards characters adapts the strategy of the supporting reading (Stroustrup, 2024, section 6.7). Acceptance boundaries, serious-failure handling, and activities are original to this learning path.
